facts.statement: Mixosaurus lived during the Middle Triassic, from about 247 to 242 million years ago.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Triassic(Anisian to Ladinian, about 247–242 Mya)

facts.statement: Fossils of Mixosaurus have been discovered near the Italy-Switzerland border and in South China.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found near the Italy–Switzerland border and in South China.

facts.statement: The genus Mixosaurus was named in 1887 by George H. Baur.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 1887 by George H. Baur.

facts.statement: The name Mixosaurus means "Mixed Lizard" because it represents a transitional form between eel-shaped and dolphin-shaped ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: The name means "Mixed Lizard", and was chosen because it appears to have been a transitional form between the eel-shaped ichthyosaurs such as Cymbospondylus and the later dolphin-shaped ichthyosaurs, such as Ichthyosaurus.

facts.statement: Mixosaurus was a small ichthyosaur measuring between 73 and 100 cm in length and weighing 2.2 to 5.7 kg.
facts.quote: Mixosaurus was a small ichthyosaur, measuring 73 - 100 cm long and weighing 2.2 - 5.7 kg.

facts.statement: The largest known specimens of Mixosaurus would have measured over 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: The largest specimens would have measured over 2 m in length.

facts.statement: Each toe of Mixosaurus had more individual bones than usual in reptiles, and its front limbs were longer than its back limbs, adaptations typical of later ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Noteworthy, however, is that each toe had more individual bones than is usual in reptiles, and the front limbs were longer than the back limbs, both adaptations typical of later ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: Mixosaurus had narrow jaws with several sharp teeth, ideal for catching fish.
facts.quote: The jaws were narrow, with several sharp teeth, that would have been ideal for catching fish.

facts.statement: Mixosaurus had relatively large skulls compared to its body, resembling later fish-shaped ichthyosaurs rather than basal forms.
facts.quote: They had relatively large skulls compared to their bodies, unlike the basal ichthyosaurs, but resembled fish-shaped ichthyosaurs that appeared later.

facts.statement: The sagittal crest on Mixosaurus cornalianus indicates it had exceptionally strong jaw muscles.
facts.quote: This indicates that it had exceptionally strong jaw muscles.

facts.statement: In 2024, a new species, Mixosaurus luxiensis, was named by Ye-Wei Fang and coauthors, with HFUT HL-21-08-002 as the holotype and only known specimen.
facts.quote: In 2024, Ye-Wei Fang and coauthors named a new species, M. luxiensis, with HFUT HL-21-08-002 being the holotype and only known specimen.

facts.statement: The holotype of Mixosaurus luxiensis was found in the Upper Member of the Guanling Formation in Luxi County, Yunnan Province, China.
facts.quote: This specimen, a largely complete but disarticulated skeleton, was found in the Upper Member of the Guanling Formation in Luxi County, Yunnan Province, China; the species name refers to this county.

facts.statement: Mixosaurus panxianensis was discovered in the Middle Triassic of Guizhou Province, China.
facts.quote: M. panxianensis was discovered in the Middle Triassic of the Guizhou Province, China.

facts.statement: Mixosaurus panxianensis is distinguished by a long sagittal crest and a lack of external contact between the jugal and quadratojugal bones.
facts.quote: The specimens found have important mixosaurid characteristics such as a long sagittal crest along the top of the skull but is seen as a different species because there is no external contact between the jugal and the quadratojugal.

facts.statement: Recently, Mixosauridae has been separated into Mixosaurinae and the sister group Phalarondontinae.
facts.quote: Most recently, Mixosauridae has been separated into Mixosaurinae and the sister group Phalarondontinae.

facts.statement: Mixosaurus species declared as nomina dubia due to insufficient descriptions include M. maotaiensis, M. helveticus, M. timorensis, M. major, and M. nordenskioeldii.
facts.quote: Mixosaurus species declared as nomina dubia, meaning the description was insufficient to fully classify them as species, are M. maotaiensis, M. helveticus, M. timorensis, M. major, and M. nordenskioeldii.

facts.statement: Mixosaurus fossils have been found in various regions worldwide, including China, Timor, Indonesia, Italy, Spitsbergen, Svalbard, Canada, and the United States, making it one of the most common Triassic ichthyosaur genera.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se han encontrado en varias regiones del mundo - China, Timor, Indonesia, Italia, Spitsbergen, Svalbard, Canadá y Estados Unidos (en Alaska y Nevada) y fue uno de los géneros más comunes de ictiosaurios del Triásico.

facts.statement: Mixosaurus had nearly 50 vertebrae in front of the pelvic girdle, about twice as many as terrestrial diapsids.
facts.quote: Tenía cerca de 50 vértebras en frente de la cintura pélvica, cerca del doble de las que tienen los diápsidos terrestres.

facts.statement: Three species of Mixosaurus are recognized: Mixosaurus cornalianus, Mixosaurus panxianesis, and Mixosaurus kuhnschnyderi.
facts.quote: Hay tres especies de Mixosaurus reconocidas, Mixosaurus cornalianus, Mixosaurus panxianesis y Mixosaurus kuhnschnyderi

facts.statement: The recognized species share similar cranial and postcranial skeletal features, with main morphological differences appearing in the dental region.
facts.quote: Estas comparten muchas características similares en el esqueleto craneal y postcraneal, y las principales diferencias morfológicas aparecen en la región dental

facts.statement: Mixosaurus cornalianus possessed a sagittal crest associated with the expansion of the upper temporal fenestra.
facts.quote: Mixosaurus cornalianus tenía una cresta sagital asociada con la expansión de la fenestra temporal superior

facts.statement: The skull structure indicates that Mixosaurus cornalianus had exceptionally strong jaw muscles.
facts.quote: Esto indica que tenía músculos mandibulares excepcionalmente fuertes

facts.statement: Many specimens of Mixosaurus cornalianus have been found in Middle Triassic strata of Monte San Giorgio and the Ticino area between Italy and Switzerland.
facts.quote: Muchos especímenes de Mixosaurus cornalianus han sido hallados en los estratos del Triásico Medio del Monte San Giorgio y el área de Ticino entre las fronteras de Italia y Suiza

facts.statement: Mixosaurus cornalianus is the only Triassic ichthyosaur for which completely articulated skeletons have been found.
facts.quote: Mixosaurus cornalianus es el único ictiosaurio del Triásico del cual se han hallado esqueletos completamente articulados

facts.statement: Mixosaurus panxianensis was discovered in Middle Triassic strata of Guizhou province, China.
facts.quote: M. panxianensis fue descubierto en estratos del Triásico Medio de la provincia de Guizhou, China

facts.statement: Specimens of Mixosaurus panxianensis possess important mixosaurid characteristics, including a long sagittal crest along the top of the skull.
facts.quote: Los especímenes hallados tienen importantes características de los mixosáuridos como una larga cresta sagital a lo largo de la parte superior del cráneo

facts.statement: Mixosaurus panxianensis is considered a distinct species because it lacks external contact between the jugal and quadratojugal bones.
facts.quote: pero es considerado como una especie diferente debido a que no tiene un contacto externo entre los huesos yugal y el cuadratoyugal

facts.statement: Articulated skeletons of Mixosaurus panxianensis have been found, and they possess vertebral centra that are taller than they are long.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado esqueletos articulados y poseen centros de las vértebras más altos que largos

facts.statement: The vertebral structure of Mixosaurus panxianensis provides evidence of a transitional position between basal Early Triassic ichthyosaurs and more derived Jurassic and Cretaceous species.
facts.quote: Esto es evidencia de una posición transicional entre los ictiosaurios basales del Triásico Inferior y las especies más derivadas del Jurásico y el Cretácico

facts.statement: The family Mixosauridae has been split into the subfamily Mixosaurinae and its sister group, the Phalarondontinae.
facts.quote: La familia Mixosauridae ha sido separada en la subfamilia Mixosaurinae y su grupo hermano, los Phalarondontinae

facts.statement: The subfamily Mixosaurinae includes the species Mixosaurus cornalianus, Mixosaurus kuhnschnyderi, and Mixosaurus panxianensis.
facts.quote: El primero abarcaría a las especies de Mixosaurus, M. cornalianus, M. kuhnschnyderi y M. panxianensis

facts.statement: Several species of Mixosaurus have been declared nomen dubium because their scientific descriptions are insufficient for secure classification.
facts.quote: Hay una serie de especies de Mixosaurus que han sido declaradas como nomen dubium

facts.statement: The species declared nomen dubium include M. maotaiensis, M. helveticus, M. timorensis, M. major, and M. nordenskioeldii.
facts.quote: estas son M. maotaiensis, M. helveticus, M. timorensis, M. major y M. nordenskioeldii

facts.statement: The genus Mixosaurus was named by Baur in 1887.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Mixosaurus (genus), Baur 1887

facts.statement: Mixosaurus belongs to the family Mixosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Mixosauridae

facts.statement: Mixosaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: A pregnant specimen of Mixosaurus panxianensis preserved with at least 11 fetuses was described from the Middle Triassic Guanling Formation in China.
facts.quote: A gravid specimen of Mixosaurus panxianensis preserved with remains of a least 11 fetuses is described from the Middle Triassic (Anisian) strata of the Guanling Formation (China) by Gu et al. (2026)

rejected.statement: Mixosaurus possessed paddle-like limbs with five toes each, unlike the three toes found in later ichthyosaurs.
rejected.quote: The paddle-like limbs were made up of five toes each, unlike the three toes found in later Ichthyosaurs.
